item.title: Dice Have No Eyes
item.description:
Title: Dice Have No Eyes
Genre: Casual , Indie , Strategy
Developer: Franek , Max Cahill
Publisher: Franek
Release Date: Nov 20, 2026
Early Access Release Date: May 19, 2026




About This Game

You're smart. You roll few dice, get few points. It's enough. Time to bank... but wait-

You're smarter. One more roll. Perfect, double your points. Just one more.

You're a genius. You keep winning. You're the chosen one. The dice love you. One more roll and you take it all.

You're stupid. You lose it all. You swear they're judging you.

Restart.

▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

Dice Have No Eyes is a dice-rolling Balatro-like fever dream about greed management.

Every roll carries a chance for glory.

But every roll carries a risk of bust.

Improve and swap your dice with each cleared level.

Collect trinkets and discover broken synergies.

Features:

  • 100+ trinkets

  • 40+ spells and snacks

  • RNG powered by God n' Fate engine

  • Magic dice effects

  • 13 companions with unique powers

  • Pretty decent art

  • Dice with no eyes whatsoever

  • Advanced tickle mechanic technology

  • Night mode for your poor tired eyes

  • 5 dreamy worlds to play in

  • An entity claiming to be God

  • Music sourced straight from starving indie musicians



Made by two guys

item.title: Rock Band Simulator
item.description:
Title: Rock Band Simulator
Genre: Action , Indie , Simulation
Developer: KONTRĀST MEDIA
Publisher: PlayWay S.A.
Release Date: Nov 20, 2026




About This Game

Rock Band Simulator is a first-person rock band life sim set in a rough 1990s neighbourhood. You’re the lead guitarist. You’ve got two bandmates, barely any money, and seven days to make something of it.

Rehearse. Find better equipment. Get on stage. That’s the plan, anyway. You still need to pay for all of it, and the people offering work aren’t big on details.

At 21:00 , you’ve still got a show.

Get your equipment together and play rhythm-based concerts. Choose what comes next, control the flow of the set, and decide when to call it a night.

A good gig builds your reputation. A bad one gives the guys something to argue about on the way home.

The amp’s fucked. Another one costs money. Time to find some work.

Collect cans. Take odd jobs. Try your luck at blackjack. You could spend the afternoon earning what you need, or convince yourself you’re one good hand away.

Someone always knows a quicker way to make money.

Meet the locals and take on jobs that get harder to explain the further you get into them. Sneak past cameras, get your hands dirty, and try to leave before anyone starts asking questions.

You probably should’ve asked a few yourself.

Have a drink. Get into an argument. Find out how many other people want to be involved.

Fight, block, and use whatever’s lying around. Between underground fights, gangsters, and the police, there are plenty of ways to lose the rest of your afternoon.

You need those hands for the concert.

Explore Ashport, a neighbourhood of bars, back rooms, garages, and people with something for you to do. Follow main quests, pick up side jobs, stumble into strange encounters, and deal with whoever’s waiting around the next corner.

When it all gets too much, head somewhere quiet.

See how that goes.

Evgen’s on bass. Diman’s on drums. You’ll need both of them in the same place, preferably conscious.

Between gigs and whatever happened on the way back, upgrade and customise your garage. Give the band a place worth coming home to.

Collect posters, take photos, and grow your in-game social media following. Fill the garage with things you’ve earned.

Some of them legally.

Forget health bars. Get used to the Adrenaline (ADR) System .

Hit harder in the sweet spot. Push too far and you’re going down. Beer, cigarettes, and other substances affect your condition, so pay attention to what you’re putting into yourself.

You’ve still got the rest of the day to get through.

Each day brings new quests, side jobs, random events, and mini-bosses. Your reputation grows, relationships change, and new opportunities turn up. Some might even help.

Where you end up depends on how you get through the week. There’s more than one ending waiting.

For now, find the guys. Get your gear.

You’ve still got a show at 21:00 .

Have the breakdown after.

Mature Content Description

The developers describe the content like this:

Rock Band Simulator is a crude comedy about a garage band. It contains strong language, crude sexual humour and innuendo, stylised drawn pin-up posters and playing cards, smoking, heavy drinking and drug use (cannabis and fictional substances), street fights with blood and firearms, and a scene where an axe can take limbs off defeated enemies.



System Requirements

Windows

    Minimum:
    • OS: Windows 10 64-bit
    • Processor: Intel Core i3-6100 / AMD Ryzen 3 1200
    • Memory: 4 GB RAM
    • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 750 Ti / AMD RX 460 (2 GB VRAM, DirectX 11)
    • DirectX: Version 11
    • Storage: 2 GB available space
    Recommended:
    • OS: Windows 10/11 64-bit
    • Processor: Intel Core i5-8400 / AMD Ryzen 5 2600
    • Memory: 8 GB RAM
    • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 / AMD RX 580 (4 GB VRAM)
    • DirectX: Version 11
    • Storage: 2 GB available space

item.title: Warlords IV: Heroes of Etheria
item.description:
Title: Warlords IV: Heroes of Etheria
Genre: Strategy
Developer: Infinite Interactive
Publisher: SNEG
Franchise: Warlords
Release Date: Nov 20, 2026




About This Game

FOR THOSE WHO WANT MORE THAN ADVENTURE!

Warlords IV is a unique blend of role-playing and turn-based strategy gaming. The game centers around your hero, who plays a pivotal role in the success or failure of your military and economic efforts.

Warlords IV is set in the troubled land of Etheria. Old foes such as Dwarves, Elves and Orcs have resumed their ancient hostilities and the Undead legions of Lord Bane have returned. The Sirians continue their quest for dominance, and the unquiet whispers speak of the Volturnans, a race even more evil than the Undead.

Now is the time for the races of Etheria to come together and engage in the final battle between Good and Evil. It is a time for Heroes!

BACK ON MODERN SYSTEMS

Originally released in 2003, Warlords IV: Heroes of Etheria is a turn-based fantasy strategy game by Infinite Interactive, designed by series creator Steve Fawkner. The final mainline entry in the long-running Warlords series, it streamlined the formula into fast, tactical battles. Now available for the first time on Steam, it runs smoothly on modern systems and builds on the work of the Warlords community.

FEATURES

  • A tactical combat system that lets you watch the results of your armies in action

  • A strategic, non-linear campaign plus random maps and a wide variety of victory conditions deliver a game with great replay value

  • 10 races and 60 units for epic battle

  • Five spheres of magic to master

  • Thorough and resourceful AI at both strategic and tactical levels

ENHANCEMENTS

  • Runs smoothly on modern Windows systems

  • Plays in 16:9 borderless widescreen, with improved Alt+Tab behaviour

  • Supports modern resolutions, including 4K

  • Built on top of the community fixes from patch 1.05b

  • Includes the community-made Amthor campaign: ten bonus scenarios, shipped in the Extras folder

  • Ships with the community-made Warlord & Retinue Editor

  • Added Steam Cloud support and Steam Achievements

item.title: IT THINKS! - Build Your Own GPU
item.description:
Title: IT THINKS! - Build Your Own GPU
Genre: Indie , Simulation , Strategy
Developer: Catchy
Publisher: Catchy
Franchise: IT Series
Release Date: Nov 19, 2026




About This Game

From one logic gate to a computer.


IT THINKS! is a hands-on hardware puzzle game about building a computer from the ground up. Place parts, draw wires, watch signals move, and prove each design on a live test bench. Your first component is NAND: a tiny logic gate with two inputs and one output. From there, your designs grow into arithmetic, memory, a programmable processor, parallel cores, matrix multiplication, and finally a chip that recognizes the shapes you draw.

Every part can be built from NAND, or licensed from the factory when you would rather keep moving, and you can always come back and build it yourself.

Build it. Test it. Ship it.


  • Complete 62 handcrafted contracts across six eras, from a small workshop to an AI lab.
  • Turn working circuits into reusable chips and build a catalogue of components you designed yourself.
  • Program the hardware you built with a compact assembly language and run the same kernel across many cores.
  • Balance real architectural trade-offs such as area, speed, memory bandwidth, power, and parallel efficiency.
  • Learn at your own pace with optional hints, short concept lessons, the Master's Notebook, and tests that let you skip what you already know.
  • Show off every solution with exportable die views and looping GIF captures.

No electrical-engineering background is required. You learn by building: try something, see what happened, and improve it.

Beyond the campaign


  • Build your own devices on the free bench. Add buttons, a keypad, seven-segment displays, a 16×16 lamp matrix, a buzzer, and dice, then switch to the front panel and use what you made. A bench holds up to 4,000 parts.
  • Share a device with a link. Anyone who opens it can press its buttons in a browser, with no account.
  • Take client orders between contracts and grow your workshop through nine levels.
  • Solve a new puzzle every day and see where your design ranks.
  • Play community puzzles and publish your own.

Coming from the demo? Your progress carries into the full game: automatically from the Steam demo, or with a save file from the browser demo.

Make it comfortable: six colour palettes or your own, a choice of typefaces including two high-legibility fonts, and full controller support.

Languages: The interface, lessons, and all in-game text are available in all 22 languages listed on the store page.

We taught sand to think.

AI Generated Content Disclosure

The developers describe how their game uses AI Generated Content like this:

In-game art and music are not AI-generated. The music is a licensed
soundtrack by a human composer.

AI-generated content appears in the following places:
- Localization: 21 languages were translated with AI assistance and then reviewed.
- Trailers: the current trailers were made during the demo period and
still contain AI-generated images and AI-generated music that are no
longer in the game. New trailers are in production and will replace them.

More details: https://steamcommunity.com/app/5196330/discussions/0/571554017506762270/



System Requirements

item.title: Blacksmith Master
item.description:
Title: Blacksmith Master
Genre: Simulation , Strategy
Developer: Untitled Studio
Publisher: Hooded Horse
Release Date: Nov 19, 2026
Early Access Release Date: May 15, 2025




About This Game

Blacksmith Master puts you in charge of your own medieval forge and has you manage resource acquisition and refinement alongside the production and sale of finished goods. Find and hire the best staff for each respective step of the process and equip them with the right tools to optimize your business and train their skills over time. Design your shop for the best throughput, fulfill orders from across the kingdom to unlock new capabilities, and seek out new opportunities in the market as customers come in looking for a variety of historically inspired items – from weapons and armor to tools and cooking utensils, you’ll perfect your craft to become the Blacksmith Master.

Tucked away through the winding alleys of a small medieval town lies your workshop – at first just a humble place for a humble blacksmith, but with potential for greatness. From here you control the entire production chain – take charge of distant woodcutter camps and mines to acquire raw materials, smelting your ores into ingots and then crafting weapons, armor, tools, and jewelry to put on display and sell to customers for a profit.

Fulfill orders from different parts of the kingdom to unlock new privileges and capabilities, including the ability to design new products. Design your shop to make the best use of space, ensuring there’s enough room for the production and sale of goods alike, all while adding personal touches to liven up an otherwise dreary space. As your reputation grows, so too will your operation, and it won’t be long before you become a master of your craft.

Be it a footman’s sword, a woodsman’s ax, or an inn keeper’s frying pan, everything you produce will require raw materials either dug up from the earth, or acquired from the deep woods spread around the kingdom. Hire miners and woodcutters, equip them appropriately, and build up their camps to ensure they remain efficient – without them, you won’t be able to produce any finished goods.

So will you invest in rest stations and additional staff at these distant outposts, spending time and money to keep your workers healthy and happy? Or will you minimize these frivolous costs to maximize profits at every corner? Perhaps your money is better spent hiring and paying the wages of talented smiths at your shop itself? And there’s always the need to upgrade your shop to include multiple storeys and more advanced manufacturing methods allowing you to craft more interesting items that in turn build up your reputation and draw a bigger crowd…

Whether you take direct control and get your hands dirty at the forge or instead rely entirely on your staff to get the job done, there will be many different ways to craft items in Blacksmith Master – some will require a longer process which includes heating an ingot, hammering it on an anvil, tempering it, assembling parts, and finally sharpening it on a grinding wheel. Other items will be simpler to make, requiring fewer tools as well as less effort and time, though they might sell for a smaller profit margin and do less for your reputation as a result.

Your job will be to research and develop exciting new goods for people to buy as you optimize your workspace to ensure your team of blacksmiths can work in tandem, creating goods from the simple to the highly complex, servicing customers from and around your small town with items like:

  • Military equipment - a multitude of weapons, shields, and armor.

  • Siege machines - put your workshop to the test with complex projects of over 100 pieces, like catapults, rams, cannons, and ballistas.

  • Kitchen utensils - spoons, forks, pots, cauldrons and everything in between.

  • Tools - from axes to hammers, take your pick!

  • Jewelry - necklaces, rings, bracelets, and crowns all fetch a handsome price.

  • Plus many others!

Different blacksmiths will have different skills that you need to cultivate. Some will be great at working with metal, others will be talented with woodwork, and others still might be particularly proficient with gems or excel at researching new techniques and items. WIth your guidance, your staff will grow more skilled over time. Will you train them as generalists, ensuring they all have support when needed, or will you seek to train famed specialists?

Other items will be simpler to make, requiring fewer tools as well as less effort and time, though they might sell for a smaller profit margin and do less for your reputation as a result.

Your job will be to research and develop exciting new goods for people to buy as you optimize your workspace to ensure your team of blacksmiths can work in tandem, creating goods from the simple to the highly complex, servicing customers from and around your small town with items like:

  • Military equipment - a multitude of weapons, shields, and armor.

  • Siege machines - put your workshop to the test with complex projects of over 100 pieces, like catapults, rams, cannons, and ballistas.

  • Kitchen utensils - spoons, forks, pots, cauldrons and everything in between.

  • Tools - from axes to hammers, take your pick!

  • Jewelry - necklaces, rings, bracelets, and crowns all fetch a handsome price.

  • Plus many others!

Different blacksmiths will have different skills that you need to cultivate. Some will be great at working with metal, others will be talented with woodwork, and others still might be particularly proficient with gems or excel at researching new techniques and items. WIth your guidance, your staff will grow more skilled over time. Will you train them as generalists, ensuring they all have support when needed, or will you seek to train famed specialists?
